title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). π is a group and ρ is an automorphism of π with ρ^n = id. This gives a semidirect product π̃ = π ⋊ Z/nZ, an extension 1→π→π̃→Z/n→1, and a canonical splitting 1 ↦ ρ. In π̃ we have ρ(g) = ρgρ^{-1}. Splittings correspond to lifts ρ' = ρ'_g = gρ (g∈π) of the generator with (gρ)^n = 1. This is equivalent to the norm equation (8): g·ρ(g)·…·ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1, i.e. g defines a 1-cocycle of Z/n with values in the nonabelian group π.

This page.
- π acts on splittings by conjugation, hence on the set of lifts ρ'_g satisfying (6).
- The computation is α(gρ)α^{-1} = αgρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}ρ = (αgρ(α)^{-1})ρ, i.e. αρ'_gα^{-1} = ρ'_{αgρ(α)^{-1}} (9).
- So conjugation of splittings becomes the 'ρ-twisted conjugation' action θ_ρ(α): g ↦ αgρ(α)^{-1} on solutions of (8) (10).
- Hence conjugacy classes of splittings correspond to ρ-conjugacy classes of solutions of (8). This is the nonabelian H^1(Z/n, π).
- The trivial class, that of the canonical splitting g=1, is parametrized by the coboundaries g = αρ(α)^{-1} (11).
- The page ends by starting the stabilizer question, completed on the next page: the stabilizer of g is the centralizer of gρ in π.

Purpose. This is a digression on 1-cocycles of cyclic groups, within the 'équation des lacets' / rotations material. It serves to interpret the order-2 and order-3 relations satisfied by Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type elements (e.g. f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and the cyclic 3-term relation) as cocycle (splitting) conditions for finite cyclic subgroups acting on a fundamental group. Their classification up to conjugacy is then the nonabelian H^1.
errors: No mathematical errors. The identity αgρα^{-1} = (αgρ(α)^{-1})ρ is correctly derived.
The crossed-out opening lines are abandoned starts, not errors.

ideas.what: Splittings of a semidirect product π⋊Z/n ↔ elements gρ of order n ↔ solutions of the norm equation g ρ(g)…ρ^{n-1}(g)=1
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian 1-cocycles of a cyclic group (norm condition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne, ch. I §5; folklore)
ideas.where_published: Standard in Serre's Cohomologie galoisienne; Grothendieck treats nonabelian H^1 / torsors in general (e.g. Tôhoku-era work, SGA1)

ideas.what: Conjugation of splittings ↔ twisted conjugation g↦αgρ(α)^{-1}; trivial class = coboundaries αρ(α)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1(Z/n, π) as ρ-twisted conjugacy classes (Reidemeister/twisted conjugacy)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Serre; Reidemeister classes in Nielsen theory)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine textbook derivation of nonabelian H^1 of a finite cyclic group via splittings and twisted conjugacy. Its only interest is its role in Grothendieck's treatment of the 'équation des lacets'. The interpretation of GT-type relations as cyclic cocycle conditions is itself known in the GT literature.
